tasks.task: Write a quote and scope from site notes

items.when: When you have site notes, measurements and the client's price list and need a clear written quote
When the client has a branded template and wants the quote costed and laid out in it
When the job can be done two ways, to show two costed options with dates and one pick
Before sending, to read the quote as the customer and list what they would have to ask
When the quote states prices, dates or guarantees, to trace each to the price list or terms
When the quote is only a price, to add real proof and honest expertise the customer can check

tasks.task: Follow up open quotes and explain the price

items.when: When quotes go quiet or a customer says the price is more than they expected
When one nudge has failed, to get a series where each message gives a different reason to reply
When the office hears the same doubts each week, to write one answer sheet with proof
Before a follow-up goes out, to cut it down and fix the subject line

tasks.task: Write a change order for extra work

items.when: When extra work turns up mid-job and needs a short note with price and time before it starts
When a customer asks for more, to compare it with the agreed scope and the team's hours
When a building job has a signed contract, to check the variation against its clauses and rates
Before replying, to check the new work is priced as new and not folded into the old scope

tasks.task: Explain a repair estimate: fix now, soon or later

items.when: When a technician's notes and a price list must become an estimate a customer trusts
When job cards arrive with fields missing, to fix how the shop takes in repair jobs
When the notes are full of trade terms, to find them and rewrite for a customer
Before sending, to test the estimate does not scare, hide a cost or leave a question open

tasks.task: Plan the daily schedule and dispatch the team

items.when: Every working day: plan the evening before, check first thing and handle changes
When jobs need arrival windows, the right technician and parts, and a sensible order
When each visit has a promised window, to order stops so every window is met
When several vans share the day's jobs, to get a low-mileage route for each
Before promising a date for a big job, to check the team has the hours

tasks.task: Write the customer message set for a job

items.when: When the business needs booking, reminder, on-my-way, late, done and review messages
Before writing, to fix how the business talks so every message sounds like one firm
When messages go by SMS or WhatsApp and need consent rules and timing
When a message reads cold or pushy, to try it in another tone with the facts unchanged
Before the set goes live, to check every time, price and promise against the client's terms
When customers still ring the office, to find the effort each message leaves them with

tasks.task: Take a new enquiry through to a booked job

items.when: When an enquiry arrives by phone, form or email and must reach a paid job without gaps
When several enquiries wait, to qualify each and draft a reply with real visit times
When customers should book online, to set open times, qualifying questions and prep emails
When the office quotes before it understands the problem, to plan the questions to ask first

tasks.task: Build job checklists with photos and sign-off

items.when: When each job type needs a checklist with required photos, readings and a customer sign-off
When the owner has a standards sheet and each role needs a job card and a missed-standard rule
When the checklist should be filled on a phone and each sign-off logged and emailed
When new starters misread a checklist, to rewrite it in the words the crew use

tasks.task: Write a customer handover and aftercare pack

items.when: When a finished job needs a pack that tells the customer what was done and how to care for it
When the pack must say what the guarantee covers, in the customer's words
When the phone rings with the same how-do-I questions, to write short care articles
When you have real customer questions and answers and want one FAQ page for the pack or site
When the job should lead to repeat work, to plan the thank-you, service dates and referral ask
When a job closes, to keep proof of what was delivered, accepted and still open
Before the pack goes out, to read it as the customer and find what they would still ring about

tasks.task: Put warranty and booking terms in plain words

items.when: When customers misread the guarantee or the office promises more than the terms give
When booking, deposit and cancellation terms need a plain summary linked to each clause
When a maker's warranty is hard to follow, to get its plain meaning and the risky terms
Before publishing, to check each plain line matches a clause and nothing new was promised
When the summary still sounds like a contract, to cut padding and say what is meant

tasks.task: Reply to a complaint and plan the return visit

items.when: When a customer is unhappy with a job and needs a same-day reply and a return-visit plan
When a message is heated, to read its tone, urgency and warning signs before replying
When the first draft sounds defensive, to get a second version that names the feeling
Before sending, to check every promise in the reply can be kept
When the same complaint keeps coming back, to find the cause and a way to prevent it
When the reply follows policy but leaves the customer worse off, to weigh the service cost

tasks.task: Reply to public reviews and ask for new ones

items.when: When a batch of new reviews needs specific, calm replies in the business's voice
On each new batch, to hold risky replies for the owner and flag repeat complaints
When the business rarely asks for reviews, to plan when to ask and how to word it
When a happy customer could give a quote for the site, to ask with three easy questions
When there are many reviews, to rank the complaints and praise by how often they come up

tasks.task: Design maintenance plan tiers and cost each visit

items.when: When the owner wants plan tiers, a worked cost per visit and the members needed to break even
When tier prices are open, to set them and decide flat fee or pay per use
When the plan needs a name, member perks, a guarantee and payment terms
When the owner is unsure how to shape the plan, to compare two models with money and dates
Before the pricing workbook is trusted, to catch formula errors and broken links
When there are two or three tier sets, to have a fresh reader pick one as a customer would

tasks.task: Launch a maintenance plan and run renewals

items.when: When a plan is ready to launch, or members are not being booked or renewed
When members need visit-due, renewal and thank-you messages in one voice
When members are billed on a schedule and need a notice before each charge
When technicians hate selling, to give them honest answers to the doubts customers raise
When the sign-up script is a pitch, to turn it into questions about the customer's problem

tasks.task: Send service-due and seasonal reminders

items.when: When past customers are due a service, test or seasonal visit and need a reminder that gets opened
When there is no follow-up routine, to set the schedule and records for each customer
When reminders go by text, to write the flow with consent and opt-out wording
Before a reminder is scheduled, to tighten it and fix the subject line

tasks.task: Set the service menu, rates and a price rise

items.when: When the owner guesses the rate, to work it out from pay, costs and billable hours
When jobs feel busy but unprofitable, to see what the team's hours earn after all costs
When the service menu confuses customers, to rate each choice and rewrite the labels
Before raising prices, to score how ready the offer is and what to add first
When the new price is set, to tell regular customers in a letter that keeps most of them

tasks.task: Write a service page and Google profile text

items.when: When the business is hard to find locally, to audit the listing and fix its text
When a service needs page copy with proof, answers to doubts and a clear way to book
Before settling the page, to see three different first screens in the firm's own look
Before the page goes live, to check a customer can book today at the price shown
When the copy is drafted, to read it as a local customer and mark each unsourced claim

tasks.task: Chase unpaid invoices after a job

items.when: Each week, to see who to chase, a reminder for each and the cash due in 90 days
When a few invoices are late, to write each reminder gentle or firm to suit the customer
When a UK business customer is overdue, to add the legal interest and fixed fee
When the customer disputes the bill, to check the reply promises only what can be done

tasks.task: Train new cleaners or technicians on the standard

items.when: When new starters arrive every month and need a job card and a day-one trial sheet
When one job type needs a tested procedure and a short deck to teach it

tasks.task: Review no-access visits, call-backs and weekly numbers

items.when: When no-access and missed visits keep happening, to find the pattern in the booking records
When jobs keep running late, to map where they wait and test one small fix
When the owner wants the same few numbers each week without rebuilding the report
Before the numbers reach the owner, to catch broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Choose or switch field service software

items.when: When the owner is comparing job management tools, to score each against real needs
When moving tools, to plan notice dates and a staged switch that drops no bookings

tasks.task: Set up a referral offer for past customers

items.when: When most work comes by word of mouth, to set the reward, the ask and the launch
When the referral ask should sit inside the thank-you and follow-up routine

always.when: Before customer-facing work, to capture the firm's voice and dated prices from its live site
Before anything reaches a customer, to catch typos and a service named two ways

helpers.when: When the job is a full price review across services, not one plan or one rate
When the owner wants more local enquiries, not only better pages and replies
When reviews are a serious problem: a low score, a pile-on or fake reviews
When messages, forms and the job tool should connect so nothing is typed twice
When the job is a multi-week build with a contract, stages and variations
When late payment is a pattern and credit terms and collections need a proper process

gaps: No library item writes a trades, cleaning or repair quote from site notes, or lays one job out as good, better and best options
No library item plans a field team's day: arrival windows, matching skills and parts to jobs, and same-day changes
No library item writes the on-my-way, running-late, no-access and job-done message set, or offers clearly different versions of it
No library item builds job checklists with required photos and customer sign-off, or room-by-room cleaning checklists
No library item writes a customer handover or aftercare pack with care steps and service dates
No library item costs a maintenance plan per visit and works out the members needed to break even
No library item writes technician and office sign-up scripts for a service plan
No library item costs one job after labour, travel, parts and call-backs to show its margin
No library item writes a change order or extra-work note for a small trades job without a formal contract
No library item checks a quote against consumer rules such as cooling-off rights and deposit limits
No library item tracks first-time fix rate, call-backs and quote win rate for a service team
